methodology: The study presents a topology optimization approach for continuous fiber angle optimization (CFAO) which computes the best layout and orientation of fiber reinforcement for AM structures. Statically loaded structures are designed for minimum compliance using the joint variable method to compute design derivatives, and a sensitivity filter is employed to reduce checkerboard effect. The layer-by-layer approach in AM is given special consideration in the presented algorithm.
research_objective: The main goal of the study was to develop a topology optimization approach for continuous fiber angle optimization (CFAO) which computes the best layout and orientation of fiber reinforcement for additive manufacturing structures.

key_findings.finding: Topology optimization approach for continuous fiber angle optimization (CFAO) can improve mechanical properties of polymer composite printed parts.
The non-isotropic mechanical properties of the printed parts depend greatly on the deposited material and its orientation during printing.
Adding short fiber/polymer composite filament improves the tensile strength and stiffness of printed parts.
The presence of short fibers in the polymer feedstock reduces print-induced warpage due to lower coefficient of thermal expansion and higher thermal conductivity of the fibers.
Topology optimization can be applied to additively manufactured structures with oriented microstructures, such as polymer composite FFF.
The SIMP method (SOLID Isotropic Material with Penalization) is extended for use in additive manufacturing of polymer composites.
